_doc: Upstream gauge registry: which gauges feed each target station, and how.
Keys are OpenFlow site ids (same format as .github/site_ids.txt).
site_id     -- daily history source for TRAINING (DWR:<abbrev> or USGS:<id>)
usgs_id     -- USGS id used to delineate the gauged area (NLDI) when building basin_zones.json
nws_lid     -- NWS gauge id; NWPS supplies ~30 days of observations and the current RFC forecast (inference + routing CLI)
lag_days    -- daily travel time used for the ML 'upstream_flow' feature: upstream_flow(d) = sum_i weight_i * Q_i(d - lag_days_i)
weight      -- relative contribution in that routed sum (absorbs reach gains / diversion losses)
lag_hours / k_hours -- hourly routing defaults (pure travel time + linear-reservoir attenuation) used by routing.py when
the recent calibration window is too quiet to fit them; normally they are re-fit on the last ~4 weeks.
forecast_days -- how many days of RFC forecast to expect at the upstream gauges (ML decoder 'upstream_known' horizon = min(lag_days) + forecast_days)
Defaults for USGS:08276500 were calibrated on the Oct 23-31 2026 flood (Rio Grande at Alamosa + Conejos nr Mogote -> Taos Junction Bridge, RMSE ~150 cfs).
Stations with an empty `upstream` list are forecast from the NWS RFC forecast for the gauge itself (mode `nws`) when one is current.

anchor._doc: Gauge below the San Luis Valley diversions. In irrigation season (Apr-Oct) most of a rise at Alamosa/Mogote is diverted before the state line; in summer 2026 Lobatos ran ~7 cfs while the supply above was ~50 cfs. Both the ML upstream_flow (daily, lag_days) and the routing CLI (hourly, lag_hours/k_hours priors) route Lobatos; after its last observation it continues with the Alamosa/Mogote change passed through the ditches (get_upstream.passed_change: the first divert_capacity_cfs of a rise at the recent Lobatos/supply ratio, the rest at >= flood_pass_through).
anchor.name: Rio Grande near Lobatos, CO (state line)

routing._doc: Hourly routing CLI only (flow_forecast.py, crest_backtest.py); the ML model keeps `anchor` (Lobatos, daily). The Rio Grande near Cerro crests a median 11 h before Taos Junction Bridge at ordinary flows (4-7 h above 1,000 cfs), and its rise is most of the Taos rise in nearly every flood, so the routing forecast routes Cerro, with a flow-dependent travel time (celerity) whose lag at q_ref is refitted each run. After Cerro's latest reading it continues with Lobatos (itself continued by Alamosa/Mogote) routed to Cerro's clock (from_anchor, flow-dependent, not refitted: a refit on the Oct 2026 flood put the Nov 3 rise ~6 h early). Nothing is diverted between them, so changes pass 1:1 (fixed_ratio). Tributaries entering below Cerro are added at full weight with their measured travel times (cross-correlation of hourly changes 2015-2026), not fitted.

celerity._doc: Lobatos -> Cerro: 12 h at 1,000 cfs, ~21 h at 250, ~7 h at 4,000 (kinematic exponent 0.4). Fitted on 113 Lobatos crests 2015-2026; matches the Nov 3 2026 rise (11-12 h at ~950 cfs) and the Oct 24-25 2026 front (21 h from ~150 cfs).

Flow-dependent travel time to Taos Junction Bridge: lag_hours at q_ref_cfs, scaled by (flow / q_ref_cfs) ** -exponent (routing.variable_shift): ~12 h at 300 cfs, 9 h at 1,000, ~6.5 h at 3,500. Fitted on 64 Cerro crests 2015-2026 (least squares + crest timing, odd/even events held out): 83% of crests within 3 h vs 72% with a fixed lag.
